sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Technology stands alone as the sole all-green, sustained leader across all timeframes with a 0.950 momentum score, while Industrials show the only positive short-term rotation.

Market leadership remains heavily concentrated at the top. Technology (0.950 momentum, YTD rank 2) and Energy (0.833 momentum, YTD rank 1) dominate overall strength, but only Technology maintains a perfect all-green profile across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD periods. Short-term rotational interest is sparse, with Industrials making the only notable advance over the past five sessions to secure the number 3 rank.

Weakness continues to anchor defensives and cyclicals alike. Consumer Cyclical sits at the bottom of the board (rank 11, momentum 0.267), joined in the lower momentum tier by Utilities (0.217) and Real Estate (0.217). Meanwhile, cracks are forming in Healthcare and Basic Materials, both ceding ground over the past week.

## Strength
- **Technology dominates breadth:** Stands as the only sector out of 11 in an all-green posture across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD periods, carrying the market's highest momentum score at 0.950.
- **Sustained leadership:** Technology has held a top-3 rank across the 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
- **Energy anchors the top spot:** Energy leads the board with a YTD rank of 1 and a robust 0.833 momentum score.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Industrials breaking higher:** Industrials gained +2 spots over the past 5 sessions to reach rank 3, backed by an improving 0.617 momentum score.
- **Momentum top tier:** Technology (0.950), Energy (0.833), and Healthcare (0.633) post the three highest momentum scores, followed by Industrials (0.617) and Financials (0.517).
- **Laggards weighed down:** Real Estate (0.217), Utilities (0.217), and Consumer Cyclical (0.267, rank 11) occupy the bottom tier of relative momentum.

## Divergences
- **Healthcare fading:** Despite holding a strong top-three momentum score of 0.633, Healthcare lost -1 spot over the last 5 sessions to drop to rank 5.
- **Basic Materials losing ground:** Fell -1 spot over 5 sessions to rank 4, weighed down by a weak 0.350 momentum score.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Core technology, energy refining, and marine shipping maintain dominant broad-based strength, while consumer cyclical niches show early recovery signs against a severe collapse in agricultural inputs.

Leadership remains concentrated in persistent winners, with only 10 of 144 groups qualifying as all-green. Computer Hardware, Electronics & Computer Distribution, Semiconductors, and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing continue to anchor the market across all medium- to long-term timeframes, preserving high momentum scores above 0.90. 

Meanwhile, short-term rotation is surfacing in consumer-facing and real estate pockets. Groups such as Luxury Goods, Real Estate - Diversified, and Medical Distribution posted double-digit rank gains over the past five sessions. Conversely, Agricultural Inputs suffered an abrupt deterioration, plummeting 104 spots, alongside continued degradation in precious metals and office REITs.

## Strength
- **All-Green Core:** Only 10 of 144 industry groups maintain positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.99), Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.97), and Computer Hardware (0.97).
- **Tech & Freight Dominance:** Sustained multi-month strength is heavily concentrated in tech and transport infrastructure, with Semiconductors (0.93), Communication Equipment (0.91), Scientific & Technical Instruments (0.89), Software - Infrastructure (0.83), and Marine Shipping (0.94) holding top-36 ranks across 1-, 3-, and 6-month windows.
- **Top Momentum Positioning:** Computer Hardware (rank 1 YTD) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (rank 2 YTD) lead all groups in momentum with scores of 0.971 and 0.988, respectively.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Rapid Short-Term Climbers:** Luxury Goods (+16 spots to rank 101, momentum 0.51), Real Estate - Diversified (+16 spots to rank 74, momentum 0.71), and Medical Distribution (+15 spots to rank 58, momentum 0.72) logged the largest 5-day rank improvements.
- **Acute De-risking in Ag & Metals:** Agricultural Inputs collapsed -104 spots over 5 sessions to rank 138, sinking to the market's lowest momentum score of 0.015. Gold (-16 spots to rank 69) and Other Precious Metals & Mining (-10 spots to rank 111) also weakened sharply.
- **Persistent Bottom Laggards:** Consumer discretionary and financing groups remain pinned at the bottom of the momentum rankings, including Advertising Agencies (momentum 0.044, rank 144 YTD), Gambling (0.033, rank 143 YTD), and Resorts & Casinos (0.076, rank 136 YTD).

## Divergences
- **Fading Leaders:** High-momentum groups showing near-term slippage include Copper (momentum 0.78, down 2 spots in 5 days), Diagnostics & Research (momentum 0.76, down 5 spots), and Steel (momentum 0.69, down 3 spots).
- **Financial Softness:** Diversified Banks and Life Insurance (both at momentum 0.61) logged 5-day declines of 2 spots, indicating early exhaustion in financial momentum.
- **Emerging Low-Momentum Rebounds:** Apparel Manufacturing jumped 12 spots despite a low momentum profile of 0.48, while defensive and leisure plays like Travel Services (+7 spots, momentum 0.41) and Utilities - Regulated Electric (+7 spots, momentum 0.38) are beginning to turn higher from depressed bases.
